newsitem.title: UK: Businesses say London unbowed by bomb threats.
newsitem.headline: Businesses say London unbowed by bomb threats.

text.p: Bomb threats will not stop firms doing business in London despite the "considerable" cost of Monday's suspected IRA security alert, the London Chamber of Commerce said on Monday.
Chief Executive Simon Sperryn said in a statement that businesses in the capital had taken the bomb threats at five London railways stations and three major airport in their stride.

"London workers and firms recognise that security alerts are an unfortunate fact of business life. Whilst the cost and disruption to business in London today is considerable, it will not stop firms doing business here," Sperryn said.
The telephoned bomb warnings caused major travel chaos in the capital for five hours on Monday morning. No bombs were found.
He said new technology, home-working, tele-working and flexitime had helped reduce the impact of the problem and suggested that more firms might consider diversifying their operations in this way.

"People must get this into perspective and not be alarmist about it. This is a problem which affects London occasionally and the capital is still a safe, attractive place to work, live and visit," Sperryn said.
